cues.en: All right. Already, already. Okay.
cues.zh: 好，好了。行。

cues.en: Thank you very much for that subtle and delicate introduction. Was much appreciated.
cues.zh: 非常感谢这番微妙而细腻的介绍，十分受用。

cues.en: Right. Well, the first thing I've got to tell you is the misnomer under which we are all labouring because ancient writing has nothing to do with codes.
cues.zh: 好吧，我首先要告诉大家的是，我们一直被一个误称误导着，因为古代文字和密码毫无关系。

cues.en: Because codes
cues.zh: 因为所谓密码

cues.en: are an artificial system of finding a writing technique which bamboozles everybody else and drives them into lunatic asylums.
cues.zh: 是一种人为设计的书写技术，目的就是把其他所有人都弄糊涂，逼得他们进疯人院。

cues.en: That is not the intention behind the cuneiform writing system or Egyptian hieroglyphs, although of course we did end up bamboozled in lunatic asylums. That's quite another matter. So this bizarre writing, if you've never seen it before, you shortly will,
cues.zh: 楔形文字或埃及象形文字的书写系统并不是出于这个目的，当然，我们最终确实被弄得晕头转向，进了疯人院。不过那是另一回事。所以，这种奇特的文字，如果你以前从未见过，很快就会见到，

cues.en: has nothing to do with codes. It is a proper functional writing system with the same purpose behind it as our own alphabetic
cues.zh: 它和密码毫无关系。它是一套真正实用的书写系统，其背后的目的和我们自己的字母

cues.en: system.
cues.zh: 书写系统一样。

cues.en: So,
cues.zh: 所以，

cues.en: it's come to my attention recently, rather
cues.zh: 我最近才注意到一件事，说起来相当令人沮丧：

cues.en: miserable in its import, that there are people in this country who've never actually seen a ginaiform tablet.
cues.zh: 这个国家居然有人从没亲眼见过一块楔形文字泥板。

cues.en: How this can be in this day and age, I don't know.
cues.zh: 在这个年代居然还会这样，我真不知道该说什么。

cues.en: But I brought one to show you. Now, this tablet is an utter corker.
cues.zh: 不过我带了一块来给大家看看。这块泥板可真是件宝贝。

cues.en: It has many immediately obvious characteristics. For example, it's written in about seventeen eighty BC, as you can obviously tell.
cues.zh: 它有许多一眼就能看出的特点。比如，它写于公元前1780年，这一点显而易见。

cues.en: It looks like a letter, but it isn't. In fact, it's a wondrous inscription and it's more interesting than everything else in the British Museum collection put together. It's rather embarrassing because it doesn't belong to us. But
cues.zh: 它看起来像一封信，但其实不是。事实上，它是一篇奇妙的铭文，比大英博物馆馆藏的其他所有东西加起来都更有趣。说起来有点尴尬，因为它不属于我们。不过

cues.en: it is written from left to right, in ruled lines.
cues.zh: 它是从左到右、沿着划定的行线书写的。

cues.en: And the writing system is a bit like printing in that you have a stylus like a chopstick.
cues.zh: 这种书写系统有点像印刷，因为你会用一根像筷子一样的书写笔。

cues.en: And you press the end of this chopstick into the surface of the clay gently, and each time you make a stroke, that is part of a sign. And all the signs in the world are made up of one or two or three
cues.zh: 你轻轻把这根“筷子”的一端压进泥土表面，每划一下，就构成一个符号的一部分。而全世界所有符号，都由一两种或三种

cues.en: designs. So once you've learned that, you can write anything. So this tablet was written by a very high quality literary scribe. You can see the front's more or less easy to read. The back looks like it's been trampled by elephants and of course, that's the most interesting
cues.zh: 图形组成。所以一旦学会这些，你就什么都能写。这块泥板出自一位水平极高的文学抄写员之手。正面基本上很容易读懂。背面看起来像被大象踩过，当然，那才是最有趣的

cues.en: part.
cues.zh: 部分。

cues.en: So this is made of clay
cues.zh: 所以，它是用黏土制成的，

cues.en: and that was the first writing system used in ancient Mesopotamian. It's a jolly good thing they did, use clay because all the tablets in the British Museum will outlast all the books and papers in the British Library for certain and every single piece of nonsense recorded on a computer will be long gone
cues.zh: 而这就是古代美索不达米亚使用的第一种书写系统。他们采用黏土真是明智之举，因为大英博物馆里的所有泥板肯定都能比大英图书馆里的书籍和纸张保存得更久，而电脑上记录的每一条废话早就不复存在了，

cues.en: and we will be the winners.
cues.zh: 到头来赢家会是我们。

cues.en: Now, I'll show you that tablet not in order to sell the book which is a tempting pile of witches in the hall outside of which our chairperson has already alluded to twice. That just happens to be on the slide. But the point is that that is the replica of the Babylonian
cues.zh: 现在，我给大家看这块泥板，并不是为了推销那本书。那本书放在门厅外，是一摞诱人的女巫，我们的主席已经提到过两次了。当然，它只是碰巧出现在幻灯片上。不过关键在于，那是巴比伦人对方舟与洪水故事的构想复原品，

cues.en: idea of what the Ark and the Flood story looked like, which came out of that tablet,
cues.zh: 这个构想就是从那块泥板中解读出来的，

cues.en: which is a kind of recipe to build it. So when you saw that, you wouldn't necessarily leap to that conclusion,
cues.zh: 那块泥板有点像一份建造方舟的配方。所以当你看到它时，不一定会立刻得出那个结论，

cues.en: but it does underline the fact that it is real writing of real language with real grammar and real meaning and no ambiguity
cues.zh: 但它确实说明，这是真实的文字，记录着真实的语言、真实的语法、真实的含义，没有任何歧义，

cues.en: and not a code.
cues.zh: 而不是密码。

cues.en: So the part that we have to start in the educational business with a map. This is the most insulting and baby like map I could find.
cues.zh: 所以，我们得从教育事业的地图讲起。这是我能找到的最侮辱人、最幼稚的地图。

cues.en: But once it shows you where Egypt is, which is that brown blob down on the left, I'm going to be talking about stuff from the blue blob in the middle, which is kind of Iraq,
cues.zh: 不过，等它告诉你埃及在哪里，也就是左下方那个棕色的色块时，我要讲的是中间那个蓝色色块里的地方，大概就是伊拉克，

cues.en: which when I started out as an Assyriologist, nobody in this country knew where that was at all. Of course, they do now for all the wrong reasons.
cues.zh: 我刚开始研究亚述学时，这个国家里根本没人知道它在哪里。当然，现在大家知道了，只不过是因为一些完全错误的原因。

cues.en: So writing began, as far as we know and definitely before in Egypt,
cues.zh: 据我们所知，文字起源于埃及之前，

cues.en: in Iraq,
cues.zh: 起源于伊拉克，

cues.en: about three thousand five hundred BC. So if any other speaker this evening floats
cues.zh: 大约在公元前3500年。所以，如果今晚有其他演讲者站到

cues.en: in front of you and starts talking about Egyptian stuff, hieroglyphs, anything like that, don't believe a word of it if they try to claim primacy.
cues.zh: 你们面前，开始谈埃及的东西、象形文字之类的，要是他们声称埃及更早，千万别信他们一个字。

cues.en: Now, the fact is this, that they used clay which was freely available in a God given way because the banks of the Euphrates and Tigris Rivers,
cues.zh: 事实是这样的：他们使用黏土。这种材料仿佛是上天赐予的，随处可得，因为幼发拉底河和底格里斯河的河岸，

cues.en: which provide the Mesopotamian
cues.zh: 也就是美索不达米亚这个

cues.en: name invented by the Greeks,
cues.zh: 由希腊人创造的名称所指的地方，

cues.en: was perfect
cues.zh: 非常适合

cues.en: for forming writing tablets
cues.zh: 制作书写用的泥板，

cues.en: without bits in it which would take sharp impressions and dry perfectly in the sun. And that's what they did. They started with clay and they lasted... They stuck with it until about the second century AD. So well, well over three thousand years of continuous use. And on the right,
cues.zh: 里面没有杂质，能够留下清晰的印痕，而且在阳光下可以完美地晾干。他们就是这么做的。他们从黏土开始，并一直使用下去……直到公元2世纪。所以，这种材料连续使用了整整三千多年。右边

cues.en: you see some reeds of the type which grow liberally in Iraq. So you got a six inch bit, cut it at the right angle, stripped off the stuff and there you had a free writing
cues.zh: 你可以看到一些芦苇，就是伊拉克大量生长的那种。取一截六英寸长的芦苇，按合适的角度切开，剥掉外皮，你就有了一件免费的书写

cues.en: tool which would last you for ages. So it was a very simple matter
cues.zh: 工具，而且能用很长时间。所以这件事做起来非常简单，

cues.en: and very fortunate that that's what we happened. So this is not going to be an exam or a test or anything depressing like that. There are two points about this lecture. Firstly, nobody is allowed to go to sleep or I shall get very angry. And the second thing is, there might well be a test before you're allowed to leave the building.
cues.zh: 而且很幸运，我们碰巧拥有这样的条件。所以，这不会是一场考试、测试，或者任何令人沮丧的事情。这场讲座有两点要求。第一，谁都不许睡觉，否则我会非常生气。第二，在你们获准离开这栋楼之前，很可能还会有一次测试。

cues.en: Now, we have tablets from almost the whole of this history. Now, these are the salient points which I want you to remember and tattoo on your wrists when you get home.
cues.zh: 现在，我们拥有几乎涵盖这段历史全过程的泥板。这些是我希望你们记住，并且回家后纹在手腕上的要点。

cues.en: Firstly, that this is the oldest writing system we know from archaeology.
cues.zh: 第一，这是考古学所知的最古老的文字系统。

cues.en: Secondly,
cues.zh: 第二，

cues.en: that it began with pictographs,
cues.zh: 它起源于象形文字，

cues.en: the old fashioned word, when you do a little picture of something to give you an idea.
cues.zh: 这是一个老式说法，指的是画一个小图来表达某个东西。

cues.en: And the kind of pictures they did were the sort of thing that talented children of three or four or most average schoolchildren do when they're 17, which is to draw a little blob for a head with an eye in it. And that's the sort of thing they did at the outset. So here you can see on these extracts
cues.zh: 他们画的图，大概就是三四岁、或者普通学校里的大多数孩子到了17岁时，有天赋的孩子会画出来的那种：给脑袋画个小圆块，再在里面画只眼睛。一开始他们画的就是这种东西。所以，在这些摘录中你可以看到

cues.en: a drawing of a
cues.zh: 一只

cues.en: jug for beer with a pointed bottom which would stand up in the ground. Next to it, there is a pictograph
cues.zh: 底部尖尖的啤酒壶，它可以插在地里立起来。旁边还有一个象形文字，

cues.en: of an ear of barley.
cues.zh: 表示一穗大麦。

cues.en: And below that, there is a pictograph which has a man's head and a bowl of food, which is the verb to eat. So this is a very simple kind of thing, such as you might expect the Martians to invent or something of the kind. And when the first signs of this kind were brought into use,
cues.zh: 另外，在那下面还有一个象形文字，由一个男人的头和一碗食物组成，表示“吃”这个动词。所以，这是非常简单的一类东西，可能正是火星人之类会发明的东西。最初使用这类符号时，

cues.en: they had behind
cues.zh: 它们背后有

cues.en: their
cues.zh: 一个

cues.en: format
cues.zh: 格式

cues.en: the
cues.zh: 其

cues.en: requirement to
cues.zh: 要求是

cues.en: document
cues.zh: 记录

cues.en: inland revenue
cues.zh: 税务

cues.en: kind of matters.
cues.zh: 之类的事情。

cues.en: They wanted to measure wages in and out. They wanted totals that added up so that really unpleasant people could come and test
cues.zh: 他们想要统计工资的收支。他们希望总数能够对得上，这样那些真正讨人厌的人就能来检查

cues.en: what really measly people had been keeping records for over the last month. So that plague,
cues.zh: 那些真正吝啬的人上个月到底记了些什么账。所以，这种灾难

cues.en: which hangs over our lives today,
cues.zh: 如今仍然笼罩着我们的生活，

cues.en: is responsible for writing at the first instance. And it was certainly not lovelorn poets
cues.zh: 正是最初促成书写的原因。而且，最开始把它变成一种书写系统的，当然不是那些多愁善感的诗人，

cues.en: who took this and turned it into a writing system so they could record their low and lewd desires for posterity.
cues.zh: 他们并不是为了把自己低俗而淫秽的欲望记录下来，留给后人。

cues.en: It was a long time really before literature
cues.zh: 其实过了很久，文学

cues.en: trotted along and somebody realised that you don't just use it for this mundane purpose, but it had this brain opening quality and real writing began and so forth. So those are the first kind of signs. They're rather clear. They're rather easy to understand.
cues.zh: 才慢慢出现，有人意识到这种东西不只是用来完成这种世俗的用途，它还具有能够开启心智的力量，于是真正的写作才开始出现，诸如此类。所以，这些就是最早的一类符号。它们相当清楚，也相当容易理解。

cues.en: Now, this is the worst slide in the world, probably. But the second point I want you to remember for your test is this, that the script evolved
cues.zh: 现在，这大概是全世界最糟糕的一张幻灯片。但我希望你们在考试中记住的第二点是：文字系统的演变

cues.en: graphically in a way which makes perfect sense. So if you look down the left hand column, those are relatively simple to understand
cues.zh: 在图形上是合乎逻辑的。如果你们看左边那一列，那些相对容易理解，

cues.en: pictographs of the first kind.
cues.zh: 是最初那一类的象形文字。

cues.en: I'll give you a clue.
cues.zh: 我给你们一点提示。

cues.en: The three
cues.zh: 上面那三个

cues.en: pieces are a mountain.
cues.zh: 部分表示一座山。

cues.en: The one below that, which is three halmer pieces and a triangle with a slit up middle, is a foreign slave girl.
cues.zh: 下面那个由三个 halmer 部件和一个中间有一道裂缝的三角形组成的符号，表示一个外国女奴。

cues.en: Get the idea?
cues.zh: 明白了吗？

cues.en: That's the sort of thing. And they had all these pictographs and basically two things happened.
cues.zh: 就是这么回事。他们有这么多象形文字，基本上发生了两件事。

cues.en: Because in the outset, in the early phases, they drew with a point much as we draw with a piece of the bior on a piece of paper with a continuous line. And that fell out of use. And they used the cut reed to reduce these curvy form natural figures, as you see on the left, into sharp angular things which consist of separate strokes of the stylus. So there's a shift from realism
cues.zh: 因为在最初，也就是早期阶段，他们用尖头工具来绘制，就像我们用一小块 bior 在纸上用连续线条绘画一样。后来这种做法被弃用了。他们改用削尖的芦苇，把左边所看到的那些弯曲、自然的图形，简化成由楔笔分开的一笔一画组成的尖锐、棱角分明的形状。所以，这是从写实

cues.en: to a kind of abstraction.
cues.zh: 转向某种抽象。

cues.en: And it's when you get to the abstraction phase that we are no longer really pictographic at all.
cues.zh: 而一旦进入抽象阶段，我们实际上就完全不再是象形文字了。

cues.en: You don't depend so much on what the sign looks like in terms of origin in order to know what it means.
cues.zh: 你不再那么依赖符号外形与其起源之间的关系来理解它的含义。

cues.en: And you can see from left to right about a three thousand year period of development.
cues.zh: 从左到右，你可以看到大约三千年的发展过程。

cues.en: If you see one end of the other together, you would have no idea probably they were connected. But the same phenomenon applies with Egyptian because hieroglyphic and demotic, unless you knew what came in between, you'd never think they were connected. But they are in the same measure derivatives
cues.zh: 如果把两端的文字放在一起看，你很可能完全无法意识到它们之间有关联。但埃及文字也是同样的情况，因为如果不知道中间经历了什么，看到象形文字和世俗体文字，你绝不会想到它们之间有联系。但从图形演变的角度看，它们确实是同一体系的衍生文字

cues.en: from a drawing point of view.
So, this script moved from a simple business of drawing pictures or ideas into a method of recording sound. And that is the essence of writing, that you have a set of marks
cues.zh: 所以，这种文字从单纯地画图或表意，演变为记录声音的方法。而这正是书写的本质：用一套符号

cues.en: which record the sound of a language with its words and grammar and all the components which somebody else can put on the record player and
cues.zh: 它们记录了一种语言的声音，包括词汇、语法以及所有组成部分，其他人可以把它放到唱机上，然后

cues.en: retrieve the words when they read it. This is a miraculous matter.
cues.zh: 当他们阅读时能回忆起那些词语。这真是一件神奇的事情。

cues.en: And the shift from pictographic use to writing sounds was the only real
cues.zh: 而从象形用法转向表音书写，是唯一真正的

cues.en: giant leaf man has ever made, apart from the envelopment of the electric guitar
cues.zh: 人类有史以来最伟大的一次飞跃，仅次于电吉他的发明

cues.en: in about 1952.
cues.zh: 大约在 1952 年。

cues.en: So this squat complacent priest on the left with a fat belly and a smug look is a Sumerian
cues.zh: 所以左边这个矮胖又自鸣得意的祭司，挺着大肚子，一脸 smug，是个苏美尔人

cues.en: of the third millennium. And he spoke one of the languages which is recorded in cuneiform writing.
cues.zh: 第三个千年的人。他说的语言之一，是用楔形文字记录下来的。

cues.en: His language is unconnected
cues.zh: 他的这门语言是互不关联的

cues.en: to any living language at all. It's quite bizarre. The guy on the right is an Assyrian who spoke the Assyrian language, of which Assyrian and Babylonian are dialects. And that is a Semitic tongue related to modern Semitic languages.
cues.zh: 与任何现存语言完全没有关联。这非常离奇。右边这位是亚述人，讲亚述语，亚述语和巴比伦语都是它的方言。而那是一种闪米特语言，与现代闪米特诸语有关联。

cues.en: So you have one writing system for two totally unconnected
cues.zh: 所以你是用同一套书写系统，来表示两种完全毫无相关的

cues.en: languages, and this is a very interesting matter. But scholars and boys and people who went to school had to learn and read the classics in Sumerian
cues.zh: 语言，这是个非常有意思的话题。但学者们、男孩们以及上过学的人都得学习并阅读用苏美尔语写成的经典著作。

cues.en: and they could get by in both. So they had a kind of symbiotic relationship between the two languages.
cues.zh: 而且他们用两种语言都能应付。所以这两种语言之间有一种共生关系。

cues.en: And this guy lives in the British Museum. There are many conundra about Sumerian grammar. I have many times whispered in his ear asking for some kind of clarity and we never get a single word out of it.
cues.zh: 这家伙被收藏在大英博物馆里。苏美尔语语法里有许多难解之谜，我曾多次凑到他耳边低语，想求得一丝解答，但它始终一个字都没吐出来。

cues.en: So
cues.zh: 那么

cues.en: this is what the time that the first tablet was written
cues.zh: 这就是第一块泥板被写下的时代

cues.en: down in about 1,800, that's what the process looks like. You hold the tablet in your left hand, you write with the stylus in your right hand and there's no way of doing it apart from that. And what is an interesting philosophical issue
cues.zh: 大约在1800年，这个过程看起来就是这样。左手拿写字板，右手用笔书写，除此之外没有别的办法。而这里有一个有趣的哲学问题。

cues.en: is that you can see a modern counterpart of this almost exactly on the tube very regularly.
cues.zh: 你几乎能定期在电视上看到与之一模一样的现代翻版。

cues.en: Now, what I find fascinating is not the implication that the thing is unchanged in all the intervening millennia. What is really interesting is that the vocabulary
cues.zh: 我觉得有意思的，并不是说这东西在中间这几千年里一直没有变化。真正有意思的是，这套词汇…

cues.en: of most people who use those pocket devices is very, very little superior
cues.zh: 大多数使用那些口袋设备的人……也强不了多少。

cues.en: to what the Sumerians were doing in three thousand four hundred BC.
cues.zh: 到公元前3400年苏美尔人所做的事情。

cues.en: That's to say, you need a small number of signs, and in the modern world, say you have 12 signs, do your stupid...
